newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asahi Breweries sees robust sales continuing.
newsitem.headline: Asahi Breweries sees robust sales continuing.

text.p: Major Japanese beer maker Asahi Breweries Ltd said on Wednesday it expected robust sales growth to continue in 1997, while its two chief rivals said they foresaw only a dribble of growth after a flat 1996.

Buoyed by strong sales of its flagship Super Dry brand, Asahi, Japan's second-largest beer company, forecast its 1997 domestic beer shipments would rise 14 percent to 190 million cases, beating the 1996 growth rate of 13 percent. A case contains 12.7 litres.

Kirin Brewery Co Ltd, Japan's largest beer maker, said it expected a much more modest two percent increase in domestic shipments this year to 258.7 million cases, although this would be an improvement on last year's four percent drop.
Third-largest Sapporo Breweries Ltd predicted its domestic shipments would rise four percent to 97.2 million cases, compared with a two percent decline in 1996.
An Asahi spokesman attributed his company's optimistic outlook to the success of its Super Dry beer.
"We saw 20 percent growth in sales of Super Dry last year and we expect a rise of at least another 15 percent this year," he said.
In June 1996, Super Dry dethroned Kirin's Lager as Japan's top-selling brand in terms of domestic shipments. Lager had been number one since 1954.
In a bid to regain its dominance in the market, Kirin this year plans to shift its marketing emphasis from Lager to its other main brand, Ichibanshibori.

Kirin also formed a special task force at the company's headquarters late last year to market its products to supermarkets and mass retailers and plans to set up similar teams at its regional operations this year, a company spokeswoman said.

The brewers' outlook is clouded, however, by factors beyond their control, including the possibility that this year's summer may be cooler than last year's or that a planned hike in the sales tax in April will slow sales.
"There is a strong possibility that the sales tax hike will have a direct impact on individual consumption," Sapporo said in its business plan for 1997.
